taxonomy:
## Taxonomy (by core mechanic), using only the provided rules

### A) Illumination / visibility constraints
- **Akari**: Place bulbs so every white cell is illuminated in row/column until black/edge; no bulb illuminates another; each white cell illuminated.
- **Kurodoko**: Color some cells black; numbers count white cells from the number to nearest black/edge (horiz+vert); numbered cells stay white; black cells don’t touch orthogonally; all white cells connected.
- **Kurotto**: Color some cells black; circle number is sum of continuous black cells extending orthogonally; circle cells cannot be colored.

### B) Loop / path drawing (single non-self-crossing loop)
- **Dotchi-Loop**: Draw a single loop through cell centers; loop passes all white-circle cells with straight-through or right-angle-turn rule per enclosed area; cannot pass black-circle cells.
- **Masyu**: Single loop through all circle cells; white circles require straight-through with a right-angle turn in adjacent cell(s); black circles require a right-angle turn at the circle then straight through next cell.
- **Nagareru**: Single continuous loop with direction; loop passes arrow cells; wind direction blocks movement against wind; special bending/entry constraints near wind cells and borders/black cells.
- **Mid-loop**: Single loop through all black circles; each black circle is midpoint of the straight segment passing through it.
- **Moon-or-Sun**: Single loop; each room visited exactly once; in each room loop goes through all moon cells or all sun cells (not both); transitions between rooms alternate moon→sun→moon…
- **Suraromu**: Single loop; must pass all “gates” (dotted segments) exactly once; starts/returns to open numbered circle; gate endpoint numbers constrain crossing order.
- **Yajilin**: Single loop; numbers indicate black cells in arrow direction; loop must not pass through black cells or number cells; black cells cannot touch orthogonally.
- **Slitherlink**: Single loop through dots; numbers indicate how many lines surround a cell; loop never crosses or branches.
- **Shakashaka**: (Not a loop) but includes “white uncovered cells form rectangle/square” and triangle adjacency counts—so it belongs elsewhere (see D/E), not here.
- **Ripple Effect**: (Not a loop) rooms with consecutive numbers—elsewhere (see F).
- **Numberlink**: (Not a loop) connect pairs with lines—elsewhere (see C).

### C) Connection / pairing with non-branching paths
- **Numberlink**: Connect pairs of equal numbers with continuous lines; lines go through cell centers orthogonally/turning; cannot cross/branch; cannot go through number cells.
- **Hashiwokakero**: Connect islands (numbered circles) with bridges equal to island number; max two bridges between islands; bridges can’t cross islands/bridges; bridges form a continuous link.
- **Hebi**: Place sequential snake numbers 1→5 in white squares; snakes can’t touch orthogonally; directional “attack” constraints using black squares and arrow direction; black squares show nearest-square count in arrow direction (0 means none).
- **Satogaeri**: Move circles within “countries” so each country has exactly one circle; circle numbers indicate how many cells it must pass through; some circles may not move; circles can’t cross tracks or pass over other circles.
- **Yosenabe**: Move circles orthogonally into gray areas; each move shown by straight arrow to a gray cell; arrows don’t bend/cross other circles/arrows; gray area sum equals total of entering circle numbers; empty gray areas allowed but at least one circle must enter.

### D) Rectangle / tiling / region shape constraints
- **Chained Block**: Black-cell blocks; consecutive black cells form blocks; each block has one number or “?”; corner contacts create chains; all blocks part of a chain; no two blocks in a chain share same size/shape (allow rotation/mirror equivalence).
- **Choco Banana**: Paint some cells black; orthogonally connected black cells must form a rectangle/square; orthogonally connected white cells must not form a rectangle/square; numbers indicate size of the area containing the cell.
- **Shikaku**: Divide grid into rectangles; each rectangle contains exactly one number equal to its cell count.
- **Heyawake**: Rooms are bold-bordered rectangles; numbers indicate painted-cell count per room (rooms without numbers unrestricted); white cells can’t stretch across more than two rooms in a straight line; painted cells can’t connect orthogonally; white cells must not be separated by painted cells.
- **Nurimeizu**: Outlined regions; each region contains exactly two blocks of same number of cells; blocks are orthogonally connected shaded cells; all shaded cells connected across region boundaries; the two blocks in a region can’t touch orthogonally; no 2×2 fully shaded.
- **Nurimeizu / Nurimisaki / Makaro / Tilepaint / Sto-stone / Ripple Effect / Suraromu / etc.**: (All are region-based but with different mechanics; see their own categories below.)

### E) Coloring / shading / black-white placement with connectivity rules
- **Choco Banana**: (also region-shape) black/white connectivity and rectangle/square restrictions; numbers give area size.
- **Hitori**: Color cells so no number repeats in any row/column; black cells never touch orthogonally; white cells form a continuous network.
- **Juosan**: Fill each cell with “—” or “|”; bold-bordered territories have numbers indicating how many more of one mark type they get; mark extension limits: “—” max 3 horizontally but max 2 vertically; “|” max 3 vertically but max 2 horizontally.
- **Kurodoko**: (also visibility) black/white connectivity and non-touching black.
- **Nurikabe**: Fill with black/white; numbers indicate count of continuous white cells; each white area has only one number and is separated by black; black cells form a continuous wall; black cells can’t form 2×2.
- **Nuritwin**: Shade some cells; each outlined region has exactly two blocks of same number of cells; blocks are orthogonally connected shaded cells; all shaded cells connected across boundaries; blocks in same region can’t touch orthogonally; no 2×2 fully shaded.
- **Heyawake**: (also region-based) painted cells disconnected orthogonally; white separation constraints.
- **LITS**: Color tetrominoes in bold areas; similarly shaped rotated/reflected tetrominoes can’t touch except at corners; colored squares form a connected network; no 2×2 or larger colored squares.
- **Sto-stone**: Rooms are bold-bordered; number in room gives count of continuous black cells; rooms without numbers unrestricted; black cells can’t connect across bold lines; when stones “drop” straight down, stones must fill bottom half with no empty cells (dropped stones may cross/connect across bold lines).
- **Usowan**: Fill colored cells; cells with numbers cannot be colored; numbers constrain adjacency count of colored cells orthogonally, with exactly one wrong number per bold rectangle.
- **Yajilin**: (also loop) black cells can’t touch orthogonally; loop avoids black/number cells.
- **Shakashaka**: Place black triangles in squares; uncovered white cells must form rectangle/square; numbers count black triangles around it orthogonally; cannot place triangles in black squares.

### F) Numbered region / block filling (counts, partitions, and arithmetic)
- **Chained Block**: block sizes and chain uniqueness; each block has one number or “?”.
- **Double Choco**: Partition by solid lines; each block contains a pair of white-area and gray-area shapes matching up to rotation/mirror; number indicates half the block’s cell count for that color; block can contain any number of cells with the number.
- **Evolomino**: Fill with numbers; board partitioned into blocks; each block filled with same number; block size equals number; same-sized blocks can’t touch orthogonally.
- **Fillomino**: Fill all empty cells with numbers; partition into blocks; each block filled with same number; block size equals number; same-sized blocks can’t touch orthogonally.
- **Five Cells**: Divide into blocks of exactly five cells; no blocks with 0–4 or 6+ cells; numbers indicate how many lines surround a cell (including outer frame); lines must surround a cell and cannot enter a block.
- **Hashiwokakero**: (also connection) bridges count equals island number.
- **Kurotto**: (also coloring) circle number equals sum of continuous black cells in four directions.
- **Makaro**: Fill empty cells with numbers; rooms are bold-bordered; each room contains all numbers up to the number of cells starting from 1; arrow cells: biggest number among up to four neighbors points to the arrow target; no same number adjacent in another room.
- **Nansuke**: Fill blank cells with digits from a list; numbers are either up-down or left-right; each cell has only one digit.
- **Ripple Effect**: Rooms are bold-bordered; each room contains consecutive numbers starting from 1; if a number is duplicated in a row/column, the distance between duplicates must be ≥ that number.
- **Satogaeri**: (also movement) circle numbers indicate how many cells they must pass through.
- **Tilepaint**: Bold-bordered tiles; color tiles; diagonal-line cell number gives count of black cells to the right or downward along the diagonal/line until grid edge or another diagonal-number cell; all cells in a tile are either colored or uncolored; solution outlines an object.
- **Suraromu**: (also loop) open circle number gives number of gates to go through; gate endpoint numbers constrain crossing.
- **Satogaeri / Satogaeri**: (movement arithmetic) circle pass-through counts.

### G) Sudoku / Latin-square style constraints
- **Sudoku**: Place 1–9 in each empty cell; each row, column, and each bold 3×3 block contains all numbers 1–9.

### H) Arrow/sequence progression constraints (non-loop, non-connection)
- **Pencils**: Mark pencils; each pencil is a straight group of cells with a tip at one end; line from tip goes through cell centers orthogonally/turning; number in pencil cell gives pencil length; line from tip goes through as many cells as the number; line can’t cross itself or branch.
- **Sashigane**: Divide into L-shaped blocks (one block wide); all blocks must be L-shaped; open circles mark the knee (bend); open circle number gives block cell count; arrows point toward the knee; number of marks in a block (arrows or open circles) is 0–3.
- **Hebi**: (also connection-like) sequential 1→5 snake numbers with directional attack constraints.
- **Nagareru**: (also loop) wind direction constrains movement along the loop.

### I) Maze / wall construction with start-to-goal reachability
- **Nurimeizu**: (not maze) region blocks—so not here.
- **Nurimeizu / Nurimisaki**: (not maze) connectivity/shading rules.
- **Nurimeizu**: (not maze) walls/maze is **Nurimeizu**? Actually the maze-from-S-to-G rule is in **Nurimeizu**:
  - **Nurimeizu**: Make walls by painting cells; create a maze from S to G using only white cells; rooms are bold-bordered; all cells in a room must be painted or left white; white cells can’t be entirely cut off by painted cells and can’t form a loop; rooms containing S, G, ○, △ can’t be painted; ○ cells lie on shortest path from S to G; △ cells not on shortest path; no 2×2 or larger fully covered by black/white.

### J) Partitioning into fixed-size blocks
- **Five Cells**: blocks of exactly five cells.
- **Evolomino / Fillomino**: blocks sized by numbers (variable-size blocks).
- **Chained Block**: blocks are maximal consecutive black-cell runs (variable size).
- **Sashigane**: blocks are L-shaped (fixed shape).
- **LITS**: tetrominoes (fixed size 4) within bold areas.
- **Double Choco**: blocks defined by solid lines (shape-matching constraint).
- **Nuritwin**: blocks are shaded connected components within regions (variable size but constrained by region number).

If you want, I can also produce a second taxonomy that groups games by **input/output representation** (bulbs/triangles/numbers/lines/shading) or by **graph constraint type** (connectivity, non-touching, exact counts, alternation, etc.).
